official.deadline_note: The African Development Bank publishes no central JADS call opening or closing date, and there is no separate application to the Bank. Deadlines belong to each partner university's own intake, as published on AfDB's own List of Universities page: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University - 'April Enrollment: October / September Enrollment: April'; Hiroshima University (April intake) - 'Preliminary Survey: Oct 18-29 / Application period: Nov 8-19 / Exam. Period: Nov 29-Dec 8' and, for the second course, 'Application Period for Apr.: Nov 4-15 / Application Period for Oct.: Apr. 4-22'; The University of Tokyo - 'Schedule A (application period: mid June) / Schedule B (application period: mid November)'; Sophia University - 'Web entry: Mid of March ~ Early April / Application: Mid of April'; Kyoto University and Kogakuin University - 'Please refer to the program website'. Current partner pages give concrete dates: APU accepts applications for April 2027 and September 2027 enrolment (for September 2027 enrolment, submit by November 5, 2026 or January 8, 2027); Hiroshima University's JADS route is October 2027 enrolment only, with an IAAS application deadline of January 29, 2027, 17:00 JST.
official.application_cycle: 2027 enrolment cycle - APU accepts for April 2027 and September 2027 enrolment; JADS at Hiroshima University is available for October 2027 enrolment only
official.status_note: The Bank publishes no central call window; intake runs continuously through the partner universities' own admission cycles. AfDB's List of Universities page publishes each partner's intake and application windows, and the partner pages currently accept applications for 2027 enrolment (APU: April and September 2027; Hiroshima University: October 2027).
official.tuition_coverage_note: AfDB, Scholarship Benefits: 'Tuition for a graduate program and the cost of basic medical insurance, usually obtained through the university.' AfDB programme page: 'Tuition fee coverage for the duration of the study program (24 months).' Partner page (APU) lists the award as 'Admission Fee' and 'Full tuition fee'.
benefits: Economy class air travel between a recipient's home country and the host university at the start of the study program and immediately following the end of the scholarship period
Tuition for a graduate program and the cost of basic medical insurance, usually obtained through the university
A monthly subsistence allowance to cover living expenses, including books

For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for research and thesis preparation; in special circumstances, computer literacy, preparatory language and other similar courses may be covered
Additional six (6) months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation

As published by partner university APU: 'Admission Fee', 'Full tuition fee', 'Monthly subsistence allowance of 150,000 JPY (including housing) (amount subject to change)', and economy class air travel between the home country and APU at the beginning and end of the program
eligibility: Should have a minimum of a Bachelor's degree or its equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering studies or related areas; and have excellent academic records and relevant professional experience, and a history of supporting their countries' development efforts
Applicants should have at least 1 year of paid employment in their home country or in other African countries after receiving their Bachelors (or equivalent university) degree within the past 3 years
Candidates should be 35 years old or younger, and in good health

Must be a citizen of one of the African Development Bank's regional member countries; applicants must not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of all types of appointments of the African Development Bank Group or a close relative of the aforementioned (mother, father, sister, half-sister, brother, half-brother, son, daughter, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew)

Candidates should gain admission to an approved master's degree course at a Japanese or African partner university - application for admission to be done directly through the partner universities - and should not be enrolled in another graduate degree program

AfDB note: 'All eligibility criteria are strictly adhered to unless otherwise communicated. Eligibility criteria will not change during an open call for applications. However, this information is subject to change between the close of one application process and the opening of the next.'
requirements: All applications should go through the partner universities, no separate application to the African Development Bank is necessary
Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program

Admission by the JADS partner university does not mean that you have been accepted for scholarship support; do not take any action with respect to your current employment or otherwise until informed by the African Development Bank that you have been awarded the scholarship
Prepare your research plan and proposal
Take TOEFL iBT, TOEC test for English proficiency

If selected as a finalist or awarded a scholarship you must inform the JADS Secretariat of any other sources of financial support; the stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if the program has evidence of additional sources of support
documents: Proof of employment for each record of employment since earning a Bachelor's degree
Certified copy of the certificate of your most advanced university degree earned
selection_criteria: Commitment to home country development priorities
Quality of the statement of purpose
Financial status and geographic diversity of awardees
Geographical diversity, gender balance, equity and inclusiveness (unusual circumstances or hardships when assessing employment experience), and financial needs of applicants
Special consideration will be given to applicants with special needs
coverage: Tuition fee coverage for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Monthly living stipend for the duration of the study program (24 months)
Air travel from the home country to the host university at the start of the study program and back home at the end of the scholarship period
Health insurance, usually obtained through the university
Additional six (6) months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation
For scholars engaged in research, a special grant may be available for research and thesis preparation
application_method: Request information and application forms and procedures from the chosen JADS partner university using the provided contacts
The candidate completes and submits application for admission
The university evaluates and selects applicants and gives them a provisional offer letter

University sends list of selected candidates to the African Development Bank and the Bank further shares the list with the JADS Program Implementation Unit (PIU) to evaluate the applications based on a set criteria
After the evaluation, the African Development Bank contacts the successful candidates and informs the universities
official.application_route: Apply for admission to an AfDB-approved master's course directly at a listed partner university and request JADS consideration within that application; the university endorses and forwards nominees to the African Development Bank, which makes the final award decision - there is no separate application to the Bank
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of one of the African Development Bank's regional member countries. AfDB's JADS news page additionally states that applicants living or working in a country other than their home country are not eligible for scholarships.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, in effect: the award targets non-Japanese applicants - citizens of African Development Bank regional member countries - undertaking master's study at the Japanese partner universities AfDB lists. AfDB states the list of universities 'will be completed with African universities' once agreements are signed, but only Japanese institutions are currently listed.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Master's-level study in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering or related areas, on an AfDB-approved course at a listed partner university. Hiroshima University notes that because JADS focuses on STEM fields, some individual programmes may be excluded from 'Eligible Courses' based on the judgement of the AfDB.
official.research_requirement: Applicants are instructed to prepare a research plan and proposal as part of the scholarship application. APU additionally requires a Research Proposal and recommends it be developed in alignment with the indicators of 'The High 5s' set by the African Development Bank.
official.duration: Two years - 'the scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less'; plus an additional six (6) months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation
official.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan, offering high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate studies at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. The overarching goal is to enhance human resources capacity in Africa in keeping with the Bank's High 5 strategic priorities - Feed Africa, Light up and power Africa, Industrialize Africa, Integrate Africa, and Improve the quality of life of the people of Africa. Upon completion of their studies, scholars are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development using the newly acquired knowledge and skills.
official.region: Asia (Japan) - AfDB lists only Japanese partner universities and states the list will be completed with African universities once agreements are finalised
official.program_type: Capacity-building scholarship programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan (two-year master's award)
official.english_requirement: AfDB publishes: 'Take TOEFL iBT, TOEC test for English proficiency.' No minimum score, test-sitting rule, validity period or medium-of-instruction alternative is published on the JADS pages.

not_confirmed: The African Development Bank itself publishes no stipend amount, currency or payment frequency anywhere on its JADS pages; the 150,000 JPY monthly figure is the rate published by partner university Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University and is marked 'amount subject to change', and other partners may publish different terms
No central JADS application deadline, call opening date or central application portal is published by the Bank
No minimum TOEFL iBT / TOEC score, accepted validity window or medium-of-instruction alternative is published
Study mode (full-time or part-time) is not published by the Bank
Deferral, renewal and appeal procedures are not published; the Bank's page notes only that eligibility criteria may change between the close of one application process and the opening of the next
verification.notes: Coverage, exclusions, eligibility, selection criteria, application procedure and partner intake windows confirmed verbatim on the African Development Bank's own JADS pages (programme overview, Scholarship Benefits, Application Procedures, Eligibility Criteria, Selection Process, List of Universities, How students can prepare); the monthly allowance figure and the current 2027-enrolment application dates confirmed on the official pages of two AfDB-designated partner universities (Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University and Hiroshima University); no monetary figure is published on the AfDB domain itself.

applicant_utility.summary: JADS works the opposite way round to most scholarships: the award decision sits with the African Development Bank, but the application itself is a university admission, so you apply to an approved course at a listed partner (APU, Hiroshima, Tokyo, Sophia, Kyoto, Kogakuin), get endorsed, and only then does the Bank decide. Tuition, the admission fee, a monthly subsistence allowance, economy air travel and basic medical insurance are covered, but visa fees, family costs, extra travel, computers and most workshops, seminars and field trips are explicitly excluded, so budget separately for those. Because there is no central call, your real deadline is your chosen university's intake window - APU's next ones are 5 November 2026 and 8 January 2027 for September 2027 entry, and Hiroshima University's is 29 January 2027 for October 2027 entry, so pick your university first and work backwards from its calendar.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A citizen of an AfDB regional member country aged 35 or under with a relevant bachelor's degree, an excellent academic record and at least one year of post-degree paid employment earned within the past three years, who is ready to apply straight into an approved STEM or sustainability master's course in Japan.
application_readiness_checklist: Book TOEFL iBT or TOEC early - AfDB names the tests but sets no minimum, yet partner admissions still require a score, so treat it as a hard gate rather than an optional extra
Collect written proof of employment for every position held since your bachelor's; the Bank asks for proof for each record, not just the current job

Get your highest degree certificate certified and keep a certified copy ready - Hiroshima University additionally demands an academic transcript, a bachelor's certificate and documented work experience

Draft the research proposal against the AfDB High 5s priorities (Feed Africa, Light up and power Africa, Industrialize Africa, Integrate Africa, Improve the quality of life of the people of Africa); APU explicitly recommends this alignment

At Hiroshima University, contact a prospective supervisor first - supervisor agreement is required before the entrance examination - and write 'JADS' in the financial plan section of the application form
Line up two professional referees and confirm they can respond on request, and format the CV and research proposal to standards laid out in the partner's own application handbook
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a course or university that is not on the AfDB approved list, so the nomination never reaches the Bank
Waiting for a central 'JADS deadline' that does not exist and missing the partner university's own intake window
Failing the employment test: the year of paid employment must have been earned within three years of receiving the bachelor's degree
Being 36 or older, or already enrolled in another graduate degree programme - both are absolute bars
Failing to declare other financial support, which the Bank warns can lead to partial or complete withdrawal of the stipend
A weak statement of purpose, which the PIU ranks explicitly alongside educational and professional excellence
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa application costs (explicitly excluded, and at Hiroshima University borne by the admitted student), any travel during the programme beyond the outbound and return flights, a laptop and other educational equipment, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops and seminars, family expenses, and any language training not provided by the graduate programme.
document_audit: AfDB asks for a certified copy of your most advanced degree certificate - an uncertified scan is a common omission
Employment evidence must cover every job since the bachelor's, with gaps that cannot be explained
The two references must be professional, not academic or personal

At Hiroshima the entrance-examination packet (research proposal, CV, academic transcript, bachelor's certificate, work experience) is separate from the JADS nomination, and the entrance examination fee is only covered by JADS if you win
At APU the CV and research proposal must follow the formats in the Graduate Application Handbook, not your own template
alerts: There is no central JADS deadline and no separate AfDB application - if you wait for a Bank call you will miss every partner intake
Hiroshima University warns its application period may close early if candidates are finalised before the stated deadline, so do not treat 29 January 2027 as guaranteed

AfDB's 2021 JADS news page states that applicants living or working in a country other than their home country are not eligible, while the current Eligibility Criteria page permits employment in other African countries - confirm your own situation with the Secretariat before relying on either
APU publishes the monthly allowance as 'amount subject to change'; do not budget on 150,000 JPY without re-checking the page
University admission is not a scholarship award - AfDB explicitly warns against taking action on your current employment until the Bank confirms you have been awarded
AfDB's List of Universities page says it will be completed with African universities once agreements are signed, but only Japanese universities are listed today, so plan on studying in Japan
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission at a partner university and request JADS consideration inside that application; the university screens and endorses nominees, forwards them to the African Development Bank's Program Implementation Unit, and the Bank approves the final award - you never submit a separate JADS application.
